description: A radiology operations manager must assign the hospital's only Saturday morning MRI slot between two inpatients and finalize the scanner, imaging protocol, authorization, and transport arrangements, with input from radiology, MRI safety, utilization review, and patient transport.

shared_context.S1: The hospital has one unassigned Saturday MRI slot beginning at 8:00 AM.
shared_context.S2: Patient North and Patient Vale are both awaiting inpatient MRI examinations.
shared_context.S3: Marisol makes the final assignment and records the imaging plan.
shared_context.S4: The radiology department's routine Saturday booking huddle includes the attending radiologist, MRI safety, utilization review, and patient transport before the slot is finalized.

PF1.text: Patient North's neurologic examination now warrants imaging for possible spinal cord compression within 24 hours, and the radiologist's required study is a contrast-enhanced MRI of the cervical and thoracic spine; Dr. Chen documented the recommendation in a personal work queue that has not yet posted to the scheduling board.

PF2.text: Patient North has an implanted neurostimulator that may be scanned only on a 1.5-tesla MRI with the device representative present; the representative is confirmed to arrive at 7:30 AM Saturday, while the hospital's 3-tesla scanner is not approved for this device.

PF3.text: The payer has approved Patient North's contrast-enhanced spine MRI only for Saturday, with authorization expiring at midnight Saturday; the approval is visible in the utilization review portal but has not been copied into the radiology scheduling record.

PF4.text: Patient North must travel to MRI by stretcher because of current mobility precautions, and a transport team is reserved to take North from the unit at 7:00 AM Saturday; no comparable Saturday-morning stretcher slot is available for a later booking.

acceptance_conditions: The Saturday MRI slot must be assigned to Patient North.
Patient North must be scheduled on the 1.5-tesla scanner.
The recorded protocol must be a contrast-enhanced MRI of the cervical and thoracic spine.
The Saturday authorization for Patient North must be recorded as active.
Patient North must be transported by stretcher.
A device-representative MRI safety commitment must be recorded.
A 7:00 AM stretcher-transport commitment must be recorded.
The clinical urgency and required protocol must be explicitly cited.

content_checks.C3: decisions['imaging_protocol'] == 'contrast-enhanced cervical and thoracic spine MRI'
content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] == 'mri_safety_check' and c['target'] == 'Patient North' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'stretcher_transport' and c['target'] == 'Patient North' and c['detail'] == 'Saturday 7:00 AM' for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: The neurologic urgency changes the assignment from an open choice between North and Vale to Patient North, and the required study changes the protocol to contrast-enhanced cervical and thoracic spine MRI.
The neurostimulator restriction changes the scanner from an unspecified MRI system to exactly 1.5 tesla and requires a documented device-representative safety check.
The payer's Saturday-only approval changes the authorization field from unverified to true for the assigned examination.
The mobility precaution and reserved departure change the transport plan to a stretcher at exactly 7:00 AM and require a corresponding transport commitment.
